# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 87 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 49 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_087_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 87

**1** Jesus said: "Wretched is the body that depends on a body,

**2** and wretched is the soul that depends on these two."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"Wretched"** — *talaiporos*: the same word Paul uses in Romans 7:24 ("Wretched man that I am! Who will deliver me from this body of death?"). The resonance is likely not accidental.

**"The body that depends on a body"** — physical interdependence — one body needing another (for food, sex, survival) — creates the condition of wretchedness.

**"The soul that depends on these two"** — the soul caught in dependence on the body-body relationship is the most compromised. The soul should transcend both.

**"These two"** — EMET preferred over "both of them" (LOGOS/PNEUMA): the Coptic *nsnoou* = "these two" — the two bodies just mentioned.

**Theological Note:** Parallel to Saying 112 which addresses the reverse: "Woe to the flesh that depends on the soul." The two sayings together condemn all forms of mutual dependency between flesh, body, and soul.
